name: rig
desc: Provides fake name and address data
why: Generates fake names and addresses from region-specific data files, an old-school utility with a quirky corner of data generation.

brief.what_it_is: RIG (Random Identity Generator) is a command-line program that assembles fake but realistic personal data. It draws random first and last names, locations, and street names from its database and combines them into a fake name and address, including a geographically consistent ZIP code, area code, state, and city. The homepage does not describe the input format or the output format in detail. The Homebrew description calls it a provider of fake name and address data.
brief.why_it_exists: The author wrote RIG to replace a poor closed-source, unattributed, public-domain MS-DOS program that generated fake identities. The SourceForge page calls it a free replacement for a shareware program called 'fake'.
brief.how_it_works: RIG picks random entries from region-specific data files of names, locations, and street names, then assembles them into an address whose ZIP code, area code, state, and city agree with each other. The homepage says the program is GPL, while the database belongs to whoever wrote the original implementation, or to the public domain if that author is unknown. Users can supply a new database.
brief.install_notes: The homepage links to a distribution page for downloads, but the URL is not given in the fetched text, so I could not follow it. The SourceForge project page offers a Download button. I saw no build steps, runtime requirements, configuration, or first-run instructions. The brew formula's executable is named rig.
brief.standout: It is an old-school, region-aware generator that keeps its data separate from its code, and the author invites people to add entries to the database or write a new one. Its ZIP, area code, state, and city are kept consistent with each other, which many simple fake-data tools do not do.
brief.status: quiet. The homepage says the current version is 1.11, released April 23 2006. The SourceForge page shows a 'Last Update' of 2013-02-18 and a registration date of 2000-01-06. I saw no README, changelog, or commit history to show recent activity.
brief.caveats: The database licensing is unclear. The author says the data belongs to an unknown original author, or to the public domain if that author cannot be found, and suggests that people who are uncomfortable with this supply a new database. The homepage gives no command-line usage, so I cannot confirm the options or output format. The last release was in 2006. The Homebrew description ('Provides fake name and address data') is a loose summary, since the project is a generator program.
quotes: RIG is a program I wrote to replace a particularly poor closed-source unattributed public-domain implementation for MS-DOS.
People are encouraged to add entries to the database.
It shouldn't be too hard to create a new one.
